The three bands fix all three parameters, giving Dq ≈ 922 cm⁻¹, B ≈ 828 cm⁻¹ and C ≈ 4260 cm⁻¹. I got this by computing term energies at trial parameters with the tool and solving in two steps.

**Step 1: Dq and B from the two spin-allowed quartet bands.** In a d⁷ ion, ⁴T₂ and ⁴T₁(2) (the ⁴T₁(P) level) depend only on Dq and B, not on C. I solved ν₁ = 8100 and ν₃ = 19 400 cm⁻¹ by linearising around a few trial points and then checking the result:

| Parameters (cm⁻¹) | ⁴T₂ | ⁴T₁(2) |
|---|---|---|
| Dq = 922, B = 828 | 8104 | 19 408 |
| Observed | 8100 | 19 400 |

**Step 2: C from the doublet band.** With Dq and B fixed, the second ²T₁ level, ²T₁(2), shifts with C at exactly 3 cm⁻¹ per cm⁻¹ of C. The tool gave it at 20 212 cm⁻¹ for C = 3800 and 21 412 cm⁻¹ for C = 4200. To reach 21 600 cm⁻¹ requires C ≈ 3800 + 1388/3 ≈ 4263 cm⁻¹. That gives C/B ≈ 5.1, which is reasonable.

**Check on the assignment.** The built-in least-squares fit (`ts_fit_spectrum`) held C at its default of 4499 cm⁻¹. It also matched the 21 600 cm⁻¹ band to ⁴T₁(b), not to the ²T₁(2) you specified. It gave a poorer fit (Dq ≈ 924, B ≈ 989, rms error about 155 cm⁻¹), so I did not use it. The exact three-parameter solution above follows your assignment.
